```{r load-lib, message = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)


```


```{r load-data}
#Read the data and read it with the correct delimiter
communities_df <- read.csv("data/communities.data")

#Cleaning up the data frame, converting "?" to NA

#Major issues with just reading this data as it is. The variable names are actually an observation for some "Lakewood city". There are 2 solutions: go through, one by one and rename all the variable names, or figure out someway to restore the variable names.

#After inspection, it does not seem like the variable names are stored in the data set. I also am not sure which headings go where in the data. So fun...

#information also seems to be stored in a strange manner.

communities_heading_df <- read.csv("data/communities_heading.data")

#time to clean up NA values and figure out what the data even means.

communities_clean_df <- communities_heading_df %>%
  mutate(
    across(where(is.character), ~na_if(., "?")),
    across(where(is.character) & !c(communityname.string), ~as.numeric(.x))
  )

```

```{r}
#lets see some summary statistics of the data. Lets check the mean.
#More of these statisitcs can be found in the "data/communities.names".

summary_stat_communities <- communities_clean_df |> 
  select(-communityname.string) |> 
  summarise(
    across(everything(),
    ~ round(mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE), digits = 2))
  ) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Mean"
  )

#Now we can see which columns have missing values, and how many.
communities_clean_df |> 
  mutate(
    across(everything(), ~ is.na(.))
  ) |> 
  colSums()
```


```{r load-data}
#Values presented in this table are "normalised" from 0 to 1. A normalised value represents where a value sits on the range. e.g: A value of 0 represents the min/smallest population, while a value of 1 represents the largest population.

#It also needs to be pivoted longer, while the "clean" data looks clean, its not fully clean. we will insert a categorical variable. We will also remove the first 3 variables and fold variable, as it is unsure how they add to the data in a meaningful way.

community_long <- communities_clean_df |> 
  select(-state.numeric,-county.numeric,-community.numeric,-fold.numeric) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(population.numeric:ViolentCrimesPerPop.numeric),
    values_to = "NormalisedValue",
    names_to = "Category"
  )
```
